parts.title: Campus Conversation: Seeing a Doctor at the Health Center
script: Listen to a conversation between a student and a worker at the campus health center.
Yes. I have a bad cold. My nose is red and my head hurts. I want to see a doctor.
I am sorry to hear that. Do you have an appointment?
No, I don't. Can I see a doctor today?
Let me check. The doctor is free at two o'clock. Is that okay?
I have a class at two. Is there a time in the morning?
Not today. But tomorrow at nine o'clock is free.
Tomorrow at nine is good. I do not have class then.
Great. Please bring your student card. And please drink a lot of water and rest today.
Okay. Is the visit free for students?
Yes, it is free. But medicine from the pharmacy costs money.
That is fine. Thank you for your help.

questions.q: What is the conversation mainly about?
questions.exp: The student wants to see a doctor and they find a time.

questions.q: Why does the student want to see a doctor?
questions.exp: He says he has a bad cold.

questions.q: Why can't the student come at two o'clock today?
questions.exp: He says he has a class at two.

questions.q: Listen again: "Tomorrow at nine o'clock is free." Why does the woman say this?
o: To say the center is closed
questions.exp: Today's morning is not free, so she offers tomorrow.
She says to bring the student card.

questions.q: What will the student probably do next?
o: Go to class at nine today
Stay at the center all day
questions.exp: He agrees to tomorrow at nine.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: How Do Bats Find Food in the Dark?
script: Listen to part of a lecture in a science class.
Today we will talk about how bats find food in the dark. Bats are small animals that fly at night. It is very dark at night, and bats cannot see well. But they can still find food.
Bats use sound. A bat makes a very high sound with its mouth. People cannot hear this sound. The sound goes out and hits an object, like an insect. Then the sound comes back to the bat.
This is called echolocation. The bat hears the sound come back. If the sound comes back fast, the object is close. If the sound comes back slowly, the object is far away.
Bats can also learn the size of an object from the echo. A big object makes a strong echo. A small insect makes a weak echo.
Many bats eat insects. One small bat can eat hundreds of insects in one hour. This is good for people, because bats eat insects that harm plants.
Some people think bats are blind. This is not true. Bats can see. But in the dark, echolocation helps them much more than their eyes.
So, remember: bats make sounds, listen to the echo, and use it to find food. Next time, we will talk about dolphins, which also use echolocation.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
o: How bats find food in the dark
questions.exp: The professor explains echolocation in bats.
Bats are small animals that fly at night.

questions.q: What does a bat make to find objects?
questions.exp: Bats make a very high sound.

questions.q: Listen again: "If the sound comes back fast, the object is close." Why does the professor say this?
o: To explain how bats know the distance
questions.exp: The speed of the echo shows the distance.

questions.q: What will the professor probably talk about next time?
questions.exp: He says next time they talk about dolphins.
